subject: Money
title: Weimar Germany
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Weimar Germany.

hook.text: In 1923 Germany, a loaf of bread cost 200 billion marks. Workers carried wages in wheelbarrows.

buildup.text: After World War I, Germany owed massive reparations. Unable to pay, the government printed money furiously.

discovery.text: Prices doubled every few days. People wallpapered houses with banknotes because the paper was cheaper than wallpaper.

twist.text: Those with debts were liberated—mortgages became worthless. Savers lost everything. A lifetime of savings: gone.

climax.text: The Rentenmark replaced the old currency at 1 trillion to 1. Stability returned, but trust in money never fully healed.

punchline.text: Money is trust. Print too much and trust dies.

quiz.question: What caused Weimar Germany's hyperinflation?
options: Excessive money printing to pay war reparations
